title: The hard question — how know this word is truly God’s
source_text: XXIII. Verum tota difficultas est, unde, & quomodo certi esse possimus hoc, vel illud a Deo fuisse dictum, & revelatum: Et quod proponitur, tanquam Dei verbum, & testimonium revera in se tale esse. Etenim verbum illud, quo credenda confirmantur, vere divinum esse, sensu non percipitur, nec etiam res est per se intellectui nota, neque etiam aliquid proprie demonstrabile, ad modum conclusionis alicujus Mathematicae, cujus contrarium plane impossibile esse mens videt & clare perspicit, nec de eo potest tantisper dubitare.
pass_a_gloss: But the whole difficulty is whence and how we can be certain that this or that was said and revealed by God; and that what is proposed as God’s word and testimony is truly such in itself. For that that word by which things to be believed are confirmed is truly divine is not perceived by sense, nor is the matter known through itself to the intellect, nor again something properly demonstrable after the manner of some Mathematical conclusion, whose contrary the mind sees to be plainly impossible and clearly perceives, nor can it doubt of it even for a little.
pass_b_english: Hard question: how know this proposed word is truly God’s.
Not sense-perceived; not per se known; not mathematical demonstration.
No absolute impossibility-of-contrary as in Math conclusions.
